new_jobs.title: Senior Staff Systems Engineer, Embedded Safety
new_jobs.description:
Boston Dynamics is looking for a **Senior Staff Systems Engineer, Embedded Safety** on the **Safer Robotics Team** . You will join a cross-functional group developing safe, reliable, and reactive robotic technologies that enable mobile robots to operate alongside humans in complex environments. In this role, you will lead the systems engineering methodology—spanning requirements generation, structured safety analysis, and architecture trade studies—specifically focused on MCU/MPU-based embedded systems and safety-critical firmware.

  

You will serve as the central technical bridge unifying hardware constraints, firmware execution, and test validation. Working at the intersection of systems engineering, embedded software, and test infrastructure, you will collaborate closely with Safety Firmware Engineers during board bring-up and driver development, as well as Staff Firmware Test Engineers building HIL/SIL validation frameworks.

  

Boston Dynamics is a world leader in mobile robots, tackling some of the toughest robotics challenges. For years, our awe-inspiring viral videos on YouTube have shown the world what remarkably capable robots can do. Now we are quickly becoming a recognized leader in automation solutions for industrial applications and warehouse logistics.

  

**How you will make an impact:**

  

* Lead cross-functional systems engineering initiatives to establish embedded system architectures, firmware requirements, and technical development plans for safe autonomous robotic platforms.
* Solicit stakeholder needs and derive, author, and parameterize clear system, firmware, and low-level software requirements.
* Establish and maintain end-to-end requirements-to-verification traceability pipelines across tools such as Jama, Jira, Git, and automated test frameworks.
* Partner closely with Safety Firmware Engineers to define requirements for functional safety features, diagnostic logic and interfaces for low-level communication protocols (SPI, I2C, CAN, UART, Ethernet).
* Collaborate directly with Firmware Test Engineers to translate safety goals and system requirements into verifiable HIL/SIL test plans, fault injection coverage, and CI/CD automated test suites.
* Guide cross-functional teams through structured safety and risk analyses—including HARA, FMEA, and Fault Tree Analysis (FTA)—to systematically identify edge cases in timing, communication, and fault handling.
Compile requirements, analysis, and verification evidence required to support a comprehensive safety case for autonomous robotic systems.  

  

**What You Bring:**

  

* 7+ years of experience in systems engineering, embedded software/firmware development, or firmware validation for complex mechatronic or safety-critical robotic systems.
* Fluent technical command of software engineering tools, including Git version control, Linux environments, Jira, and requirements management platforms such as Jama.
* Proficiency in C/C++ for embedded firmware as well as Python (including pytest ecosystems) to effectively engage with both firmware development and test automation tooling.
* Deep familiarity with relevant safety standards (e.g., IEC 61508, ISO 26262, or IEC 62304) and experience compiling data to support safety claims.
* Strong ability to read electrical schematics, datasheets, and low-level protocol payloads (SPI, I2C, CAN, UART, Ethernet) to ensure hardware intent matches firmware behavior.
* Demonstrated experience acting as a technical liaison between firmware development teams and product development teams.
Exceptional written and verbal communication, cross-functional collaboration, and conflict resolution skills.  

  

**Nice to Have Skills:**

  

* Experience with firmware coding standards like MISRA C/C++.
* Experience with static and dynamic analysis software tools.
* Familiarity with software and hardware testing for HIL/SIL environments.
* Experience with embedded Linux (kernel and user space), real-time operating systems (RTOS), and hardware debuggers/trace equipment (J-Link, Lauterbach, oscilloscopes, logic analyzers).
Hands-on familiarity with electro-mechanical actuation subsystems, including motor controllers, encoders, and power/current sensing.  

  

*We are interested in every qualified candidate who is eligible to work in the United States. However, we are not able to sponsor visas for this position.*

  

*The salary range for this position will be clearly stated in the job posting as required by Massachusetts law. The base pay range for this position is between $155,000 - $193,000. This range represents a good faith estimate of compensation at the time of posting.*

new_jobs.title: Mechatronics Engineer
new_jobs.description:
**About CircuitHub**
--------------------

CircuitHub is reshaping electronics manufacturing with The Grid, a factory-scale robotics platform that makes small-batch, high-mix electronics assembly radically more efficient. Think semiconductor-fab precision applied to the chaotic world of prototyping and low-volume production: a 10x throughput improvement in one of the world's most foundational industries.

We've raised $45M from top-tier investors including Plural, Y Combinator and Google Ventures, and we're already profitable. Our customers include a major EV maker, a top AI lab and many of the worlds largest companies.

The Grid isn't a prototype. It's live, scaling fast and delivering real revenue, and we're building the team that will scale it further.

**The role**
------------

Mechatronics Engineers at CircuitHub own projects end to end. You'll start with a problem, often on our factory floor, and take it all the way to a working machine:

* Understand the problem and turn it into a clear specification
* Generate ideas and choose the right mechanism
* Design it in CAD and prove it out with the engineering calculations
* Prototype and build it, machining parts in our in-house CNC shop
* Bring it to life with software on our in-house robotics operating system

We work AI-first. AI tools help you scope the problem, drive your CAD, run the calculations and write the machine software. The software side needs basic software engineering skills, not a software background: you'll write it with AI agents, supported by a dedicated software engineering team who build the operating system.

You must have built things before, ideally robots, whether as a hobbyist, student, employee or founder. We don't hire narrow specialists. We want engineers who can:

* Diagnose system-wide failures from first principles
* Prototype mechanical and software fixes on the fly
* Work autonomously and communicate clearly with a team spread across sites
* Take responsibility for how their machines perform in live production

**Things you'll do**
--------------------

This is a design role with hands-on prototyping. For example:

* Conceive new mechanisms to handle electronics parts and other robotic handling tasks, using AI to scope and specify the problem
* Design gantries and end effectors in Fusion 360
* Use AI agents to run the engineering calculations, and know when to distrust them
* Machine prototype parts in our in-house CNC shop
* Analyse end-effector behaviour from video and revise its geometry and control approach to improve throughput and reliability
* Program machine behaviour on our in-house robotics operating system, with AI agents doing the heavy lifting
* Specify sensors that catch errors while a machine is running, or monitor a chemical process
* Prototype and deploy a new test robot for in-line PCB validation
* Commission your machines and hand them over to our build team to scale up
* Work across our US and UK sites to share what you've learned and shape the roadmap

**Bonus skills**
----------------

* Experience programming machines, whether PLCs, robot controllers, embedded systems or Python
* Programming and running CNC machinery
* Design of chemical handling machinery
* Optics

**Pay and level**
-----------------

$80K–$200K depending on experience, plus equity.

A candidate at the lower end of the range might have:

* Built some systems before, with some exposure to robotics or automation
* Seen parts and subsystems through to manufacture as part of a design team
* Knowledge of designing for machining
* A keen interest in moving their career towards practical robotics

A candidate at the upper end might also have:

* Led the build and deployment of large-scale automated systems
* Written the software that controls their own machines
* Designed for a wide range of manufacturing methods, from machining to sheet metal to injection moulding
* Mentored more junior engineers

The range isn't a hard limit: if you're an expert in all of the above, we still want to talk to you. Not quite so experienced but passionate and keen to learn? Talk to us too.

**Location**
------------

Full-time on-site at our factory in South Deerfield, Western Massachusetts, 90 minutes from Boston, where the Grid runs in production today.

Compensation Range: $80K - $200K

This role suits someone early in their career who likes structure, asks precise questions, and wants to learn how a complex robot comes together across mechanical, electrical, software, and test.

### **What You'll Do**

* Write and maintain clear, measurable, testable system requirements, and keep the requirements register accurate as designs change.

* Work with the System Verification and Test team to ensure test cases trace to requirements and that verification coverage is complete.
* Write feature requirements documents that define how each feature works across the robot's subsystems, and help develop cross-functional design solutions with mechanical, electrical, and software teams.

### **What You'll Bring**

* Typically 0-3 years of experience in systems engineering, robotics, or a related engineering role. New graduates are welcome; 1-2 years of industry experience is a plus.
* Strong sense of ownership: you take a problem, see it through to completion, and make things happen without waiting to be asked.
* Internship, co-op, or student project experience (for example, competition teams or capstone projects) where you defined requirements, ran tests, or integrated hardware and software.
* Precise technical writer who can turn an ambiguous need into a requirement someone can build and test against.
* Organized and detail-oriented, comfortable keeping a large body of requirements consistent and up to date.
* Curious about how mechanical, electrical, and software subsystems interact, and willing to dig into the details of each.
* Clear communicator who works well with cross-functional teams and contributes thoughtfully to design reviews.
* Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Systems Engineering preferred; degrees in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Robotics, Computer Science, or a related field will be considered alongside relevant systems engineering experience.
* Onsite presence is expected at least 3 days per week at our Charlestown, MA offices to stay close to the hardware.

**Nice to Have**

* Familiarity with Jira or a similar tracking tool
* Exposure to requirements management or test planning
* Python scripting
* Experience with robots or other hardware in a production setting

new_jobs.title: IT Systems Engineer, Client Platform Engineer, ChromeOS
new_jobs.description:
**About Anthropic**
-------------------

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

**About the role**
------------------

The Endpoint team (Client Platform Engineering) manages the devices Anthropic’s people work on, plus the infrastructure underneath them. We treat the fleet as a distributed platform, not a collection of devices, and configuration ships as code through pull requests, CI, staging, and a canary group. Today the fleet is mostly macOS, with a growing mobile footprint.

Anthropic also works with vendor and business process outsourcing (BPO) partners whose teams need access to Anthropic systems. Those programs are growing, in more countries and with more vendors. Anthropic-owned Chromebooks issued to vendor staff are becoming the default device for vendor teams. This role exists to make ChromeOS a supported platform with a dedicated owner. You will own ChromeOS end to end, from how devices are bought and enrolled to how they are locked down, monitored, and retired, and help bring Android in as a second platform.

The team is deliberately lean and runs with high autonomy. You’ll define what ChromeOS looks like at Anthropic and own the platform decisions that get it there.

**Responsibilities**
--------------------

* Own ChromeOS as a platform at Anthropic: device standards, Google Admin console and Chrome Enterprise setup, organizational unit design, and policy
* Manage ChromeOS policy as code through the Chrome Policy API, GAM, and Terraform, in the team's config-as-code pipeline, so changes are reviewed, tested, and progressively rolled out like the rest of the fleet
* Build zero touch enrollment through resellers, so a Chromebook arrives enrolled and works the first time in every country our vendor partners work from
* Work with IT Operations and procurement partners on buying and shipping devices internationally, including regions our current partners don’t reach
* Design device models for vendor teams (kiosk, managed guest sessions, shared devices, and assigned devices) and pick the right one for each program
* Lock devices down to what the work needs: copy and paste, downloads, printing, USB, and app and extension controls
* Own the device lifecycle for vendor fleets, from enrollment to wipe, lock, and retrieval when an engagement ends
* Feed ChromeOS device data into our fleet telemetry, tracking which devices are checking in, OS version, and drift between expected and actual state
* Partner with Corporate Security on hardware standards (such as Verified Access attestation and minimum AUE date), device trust signals, and access decisions
* Work with Security on the contractor access model and on keeping Anthropic data off vendor devices
* Run data loss controls through Chrome Enterprise Premium
* Work with Security on the vendor identity model: which accounts vendor staff use and in which tenant
* Support Android as a second platform, working with the corporate mobile program on Android Enterprise and zero-touch enrollment
* Write the runbooks IT Operations and vendor partners use to stand up a new program

**You may be a good fit if you**
--------------------------------

* Have owned ChromeOS as a platform for a fleet of thousands of devices
* Know the Google Admin console and Chrome Enterprise well: OU design, device and user policy, enrollment, and reporting
* Have automated ChromeOS policy through the Chrome Policy API or GAM
* Have run kiosk, managed guest, or shared device programs for frontline, contact center, or outsourced teams
* Have set up zero touch enrollment with resellers and shipped devices across several countries
* Have worked with Android device management and can hold your own in a mixed fleet
* Excel at ambiguous problems that touch several teams at once
* Communicate technical concepts clearly to any audience, including vendor partners
* View IT Engineering as requiring product engineering rigor
* Write clear documentation as a natural part of your workflow

**Strong candidates may also**
------------------------------

* Manage device configuration as code (pull requests, CI, staged rollout) instead of clicking in consoles
* Have managed ChromeOS alongside macOS or mobile fleets
* Have used VDI or browser-based access to keep data off the device for outsourced teams
* Have supported BPO or vendor programs through fast growth into new regions
* Have built automated, progressive rollout systems with promotion gated on telemetry
* Have used LLMs to automate operational work, or are excited to make Claude a teammate

**Technical Skills**
--------------------

* Python and shell scripting
* ChromeOS management through the Google Admin console and Chrome Enterprise
* Google Admin SDK, Chrome Policy API, and GAM for automating policy and reporting
* Android Enterprise management (working knowledge)
* Querying live device state at fleet scale
* GitOps and CI for configuration management
* Endpoint security fundamentals

new_jobs.description:
**Job Title**

Automation Design Engineer

– Automotive Welding

**Job Summary**

You will design, develop, and test automated welding systems and robotic tooling for automotive manufacturing. Your work includes creating 3D models, selecting automation equipment, and ensuring designs meet safety and customer standards.

**Key Responsibilities**

* **Design Systems:** Create 3D models and 2D manufacturing drawings for robotic welding cells, end-of-arm tooling, and assembly fixtures using CAD software like SolidWorks or AutoCAD.
* **Integrate Robotics:** Select and integrate industrial robots, welding guns (MIG, TIG, Resistance/Spot), sensors, and safety hardware.
* **Collaborate:** Work with project managers, controls engineers, and the shop floor to ensure designs are practical and buildable.
* **Review Safety:** Ensure all mechanical and automation designs follow OSHA, RIA, and customer-specific safety standards.
* **Support Build & Launch:** Assist with assembly troubleshooting, robot path simulations, and final buy-off at customer sites if needed.

**Qualifications & Skills**

* **Education:** Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, or a related field (or equivalent practical experience).
* **Experience:** 3 to 5 years of experience in automation design, specifically within the automotive or tier-1 welding supplier industry.
* **Software Skills:** Proficiency in 3D CAD software (SolidWorks, CATIA, or Inventor) and robotic simulation tools (Robcad or Process Simulate).
* **Knowledge Base:** Strong understanding of resistance spot welding, MIG welding, pneumatic components, and geometric dimensioning and tolerancing (GD&T).

**Job Title:** Process Automation Design Engineer

– Automotive Welding Systems

**Department:** Process Engineering / Automation

**Reports To:** Engineering Manager

**Position Summary:**

The Process Automation Design Engineer is responsible for designing, simulating, and optimizing complete automated welding manufacturing lines. This role focuses on the macro-level process layout, material flow, cycle-time (thru-put) analysis, and the high-level integration of FANUC robotic arms into coherent production cells.

**Key Responsibilities:**

* **Process & Layout Design:** Develop 2D/3D manufacturing line layouts, sequence of operations, and process flow diagrams for robotic MIG, spot, and laser welding cells.
* **FANUC Robot Simulation:** Utilize simulation software (such as FANUC ROBOGUIDE or Process Simulate) to perform reach studies, interference checks, and cycle time analysis.
* **System Integration:** Define the interaction between FANUC robots, material handling systems, safety gating, and PLC-controlled equipment.
* **Cycle Time Optimization:** Analyze and optimize robot paths and process steps to meet strict automotive customer throughput requirements.
* **Specifications & Standards:** Ensure all process designs comply with automotive OEM specifications (e.g., Ford, GM, Stellantis) and safety standards (RIA/OSHA).
* **Cross-Functional Collaboration:** Partner with Tooling Design Engineers to align fixture placement with robot access paths and process constraints.

**Qualifications:**

* **Education:** Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical, Manufacturing, or Automation Engineering.
* **Experience:** 3+ years in automotive process automation design, focusing on robotic welding lines.
* **Technical Skills:** High proficiency in FANUC ROBOGUIDE, AutoCAD, and 3D CAD platforms. Deep knowledge of MIG/MAG and resistance spot welding parameters.
* **Knowledge:** Strong understanding of automotive assembly line routing, safety circuits, and line balancing.

**Job Title:** Tooling Automation Design Engineer

– Welding & FANUC

**Department:** Mechanical Design / Tooling

**Reports To:** Tooling Engineering Supervisor

**Position Summary:**

The Tooling Automation Design Engineer is responsible for the mechanical design of welding fixtures, clamping systems, and specialized End-of-Arm Tooling (EOAT) for FANUC robots. This role ensures parts are held precisely to meet tight tolerances during high-stress robotic welding applications.

**Key Responsibilities:**

* **Fixture & Tooling Design:** Design 3D geometric welding fixtures, manual/pneumatic clamping systems, and heavy-duty robotic EOAT using SolidWorks, CATIA, or NX.
* **FANUC Payload & Center of Gravity (CG) Analysis:** Calculate load capacities, moments of inertia, and CG for EOAT to ensure compliance with specific FANUC robot payload profiles.
* **Component Selection:** Specify standard automation components including pneumatic cylinders, toggle clamps, proximity sensors, grippers, and slide units.
* **GD&T Application:** Apply strict Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing (GD&T) to fabrication prints to ensure part repeatability and quality.
* **Welding Environment Design:** Material selection and shielding design to withstand weld spatter, high heat, and harsh production environments.
* **Build Support:** Support the toolroom build, assembly, shim-tuning, and try-out phases of fixtures and EOAT.

**Qualifications:**

* **Education:** Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Tool & Die Design, or equivalent trade experience.
* **Experience:** 3+ years designing physical tooling, fixtures, and robotic grippers for automotive body-in-white (BIW) welding applications.
* **Technical Skills:** Advanced 3D CAD modeling skills (SolidWorks preferred); strong knowledge of pneumatics and fluid power schematics.
* **Knowledge:** Deep understanding of FANUC robot mechanical mounting interfaces and payload constraints.

new_jobs.description:
**Job Summary**
---------------

The Space Physics Research Laboratory (SPRL) in the College of Engineering is seeking an experienced, highly motivated Electrical Engineer to provide technical and project support for current and future space mission and instrument development projects.

SPRL is a College of Engineering research facility that serves faculty, government agencies (such as NASA and DoD), and industry in the development of unique integrated systems and instrumentation that are often used in challenging environments ( e.g. space, arctic, above/on/below the water). The SPRL professional staff, with faculty and researchers, have built more than 35 space systems and instruments; instrumented numerous sounding rockets, balloons and aircraft; and developed ground-based instruments. For eight decades, University of Michigan has been one of a handful of universities able to conceive, design, construct, test, and operate space flight instruments - a truly 'end-to-end' operation.

The Engineer in Research Intermediate will develop and design analog, analog-to-digital, and power-system electronics in particular, and assume primary responsibility for the design of instrument modules and support subsystems. They will design, specify, and test hardware and software used in those systems and prepare test and integration plans for all phases of electronic hardware development. In addition, they will participate in the development of proposals for new research opportunities, participate in sponsor and project-level review meetings representing the University and principal investigator interests. They will also evaluate hardware and software designs for correctness and applicability to overall design requirements.

**Responsibilities\***
----------------------

* Design of electrical systems and analog components for instruments, including neutral and ion mass spectrometers and energetic particle detectors, ion thruster components, magnetometers and other spacecraft components and instruments.
* Ability to perform parts stress, power dissipation, and thermal stress analysis of instrument and small satellite electrical designs.
* Knowledge and experience of the testing and verification of electrical components or assemblies.
* Knowledge and experience in the proper design of electrical components for space systems, including vacuum, thermal, materials, and other considerations.
* Knowledge and experience with the challenges of the space environment and other harsh environments to inform PCB layout, component selection and placement, radiation effects mitigation, signal integrity, and thermal cycling.
* Knowledge of standard design tools such as Altium and LTSpice.

**Required Qualifications\***
-----------------------------

* BS in Electrical Engineering
* Demonstrated excellence in team cooperation, organization, and communication skills.
* One to three years of experience in the development, design, integration, and testing of electronics used in scientific instrumentation for air and spaceborne environments
* Design experience in analog electronics, analog-to-digital, power systems, and sensor systems to inform circuit design, PCB layout, assembly, and testing.
* This position requires access to technology controlled under the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) or Export Administration Regulations (EAR). To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, candidates must qualify as a 'U.S. Person,' which includes U.S. citizens, lawful permanent residents (green card holders), and certain protected individuals (such as refugees or asylees) as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), or eligible to obtain the required export authorization from the U.S. government.

**Desired Qualifications\***

* Master's degree in Electrical Engineering
* 5 years of experience in developing flight or flight development hardware for NASA or DoD applications, such as mass spectrometers, magnetometers, etc.
* Experience in analog, analog-to-digital, power system, and/or sensor design. and sensitive signal amplification design experience
* Cognizant engineer experience in organizing and planning electronics contributions for instrument and avionics projects
* Experience in the preparation of technical and cost proposals for government-sponsored projects

new_jobs.title: Experienced Controls Engineer
new_jobs.description:
Build custom machines that turn demanding manufacturing requirements into working automation.
  
  
PAR Systems is seeking a Controls Engineer with a strong Beckhoff background to join our Advanced Manufacturing team. Our systems support challenging aerospace and defense applications, including precision cutting and trimming, robotic and configurable fixtures, drilling, and friction stir welding. In this role, you will develop controls and software for custom machines where coordinated motion, process control, and reliable operation are essential. You will bring hands-on TwinCAT experience to project delivery while helping expand our Beckhoff expertise, reusable software, and engineering practices.
  
  
We welcome candidates at the Advanced or Senior Engineer level. Placement will reflect your technical depth, independence, project ownership, and ability to guide others.
  
  
What you’ll do
  

* Translate customer and machine requirements into controls architectures, software designs, and test plans.
* Develop modular, maintainable machine-control software using Beckhoff TwinCAT 3 and IEC 61131-3 Structured Text.
* Configure and commission Beckhoff controllers, EtherCAT networks, I/O, servo drives, and connected devices.
* Implement and tune motion control, including axis sequencing, synchronization, and coordinated movement.
* Develop machine operating modes, process sequences, interlocks, alarms, diagnostics, and recovery behavior.
* Integrate operator interfaces, instrumentation, robots, and PC applications with the machine-control system.
* Collaborate with electrical, mechanical, software, and process engineers to resolve system interfaces and design challenges.
* Test software through simulation and staged integration, then support machine power-up, debugging, Factory Acceptance Testing, and customer-site commissioning.
* Troubleshoot issues across software, electrical hardware, motion systems, and manufacturing processes.
* Contribute reusable libraries, coding standards, documentation, and technical reviews. Share your Beckhoff knowledge and mentor other engineers.

What you bring
  

* A bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering, mechanical engineering, computer engineering, computer science, or a related field; equivalent relevant experience will also be considered.
* Typically five or more years of controls or automation engineering experience, with demonstrated responsibility for delivering automated equipment.
* Substantial hands-on experience developing and commissioning Beckhoff TwinCAT 3 applications. Your experience includes implementing machine functionality and bringing it into operation.
* Strong Structured Text programming skills and experience organizing software into reusable function blocks and clear interfaces.
* Practical experience configuring and troubleshooting EtherCAT networks, I/O, and servo systems.
* Experience implementing motion control, commissioning axes, tuning drives, and diagnosing motion performance.
* Ability to read electrical schematics and troubleshoot interactions between software and physical equipment.
* Clear communication, sound engineering judgment, and the ability to follow technical issues through resolution.
* Willingness to travel for installation and commissioning.

Experience that would strengthen your application
  

* TwinCAT NC PTP, NC I, or CNC applications involving coordinated motion and interpolated toolpaths.
* Robotics, custom kinematics, coordinate transformations, or path-controlled manufacturing.
* TwinSAFE programming and machine safety validation.
* TwinCAT HMI or other industrial operator-interface development.
* ADS communication and integration with C#, C++, Python, or web applications.
* Git, object-oriented programming, automated testing, and reusable software-library development.
* Simulation, virtual commissioning, or digital machine models.
* Precision manufacturing, process instrumentation, force control, or closed-loop process control.
* Experience with Siemens, B&R, or Rockwell platforms.
* AutoCAD Electrical, EPLAN, or similar electrical design tools.

You do not need experience with every preferred technology to apply. We are especially interested in engineers who combine strong Beckhoff fundamentals with curiosity, practical troubleshooting skills, and ownership of completed machines.
  
  
You’ve learned about what you'll be doing, here are the benefits you'll gain when you join our team:
  

* Global team recognized for their passion of inventing
* First-of-a-kind product culture and project exposure
* Training and development from industry-leading experts
* Cutting edge benefit programs that include: 401(k) & matching; Medical, Dental, Vision Insurance; Disability & Life Insurance; PTO, Paid Holidays, & Parental Leave for both Parents; Tuition Reimbursement

With more than $1B in revenue, Tennant Company is a globally recognized leader in the cleaning equipment industry. For the past 150 years, we have been passionate about developing and manufacturing innovative and sustainable solutions for our customers. At Tennant Company, we are committed to stewardship and creating a cleaner, safer and healthier world. With manufacturing, operations and sales, service, and support functions across the globe, your journey at Tennant can take you places you never expected.

  

**Position Overview**
  
We are seeking a Principal Robotics Engineer - Machine Integration Lead to join the TNC Robotics Product Development and R&D organization. This Engineer is responsible for leading technical execution of systems & architecture integration across complex electro-mechanical, software, and partner technologies (such as Brain Corp) into TNC Robotics cleaning solutions.

The Machine Integration Lead Engineer is responsible for delivering integrated systems using technical rigor to translate the product vision into functional, compliant, and cost-effective designs. Success is measured by the robustness in execution of system architectures, integration speed, and the successful application of new technologies to complex problems.

  

**Key Responsibilities**

The Machine Integration Lead Engineer is responsible for leading technical team execution against the overall system definition & development plans, and leading in delivery of system integration events across New Product Development (NPD) efforts:

* **Technical Planning & Work Breakdown Leadership**: Lead cross-functional technical planning by identifying key decisions and linking knowledge-building work. Define system scope in a clear WBS with deliverables, interfaces, and owners. Drive technical team execution against an integrated project plan (milestones, integration events, V&V, dependencies) to deliver on commitments, escalate risks, trade-offs, and corrective actions to keep development on track.
* **Requirements Translation & Specification:** Translate customer, business, and technical requirements into clear technical specifications and linked to verification & validation (V&V) activities.
* **System Architecture & Integration:** Lead in the delivery and integration of system & sub-system level design efforts, focusing on well-defined interfaces across system boundaries, and delivering integrated designs that meets overall machine cost, performance, and quality requirements.
* **Technical Rigor & Design Reviews:** Lead cross-functional teams through disciplined design reviews that surface risk mitigation early, drive actionable feedback, and align stakeholders on decisions. Ensure reviews demonstrate requirements compliance, V&V strategy/progress, and readiness for prototype and production builds—including manufacturing, sourcing, and quality plans.

**JOB TITLE:** JUNIOR ELECTRICAL ENGINEER MANAGER
  
**DEPARTMENT:** FACILITIES
  
**STATUS:** FULL TIME
  
**REPORTS TO:** DIRECTOR OF FACILITIES
  
  
**POSITION SUMMARY:**  
Owns all lighting and lighting controls property-wide, interior, exterior, architectural, and feature, plus the Guest Room Management System (GRMS) and supporting low-voltage infrastructure. Hands-on troubleshooting, repair, and programming, with support to Facilities on daily operations and emergency calls.
  
  
**RESPONSIBILITIES:**  
**Lighting:** Interior & Exterior
  

* Troubleshoot and repair all lighting properties wide: casino floor, guest rooms and corridors, F&B, event space, retail, pool, and back-of-house.
* Own exterior and site lighting, façade and feature, porte-cochère, garage and lots, signage and marquee, landscape, and egress/emergency.
* Replace lamps, drivers, ballasts, and LED modules, diagnose flicker, color shift, and dimming faults to root cause.
* Trace and repair branch circuits, contactors, relays, and lighting panels, maintain fixture inventory and spec standards.

Lighting Controls & Programming
  

* Program and commission scenes, zones, schedules, presets, and override behavior.
* Maintain astronomical time clocks, photocells, occupancy sensors, and daylight controls, adjust seasonally, when needed.
* Support events, features, and holiday lighting, keep configuration backups and version records current.

Guest Room Management System (GRMS)
  

* Troubleshoot room controllers, sensors, thermostats, logic, control panels, drapery motors, and room scenes.
* Program, configure and commission rooms, device swap, or firmware update, validate scenes and setback before release to inventory.
* Respond to guest room calls quickly and discreetly, track and eliminate repeat failures.

Low Voltage
  

* Install, terminate, test, and repair low-voltage cabling and devices for lighting control, GRMS, and building controls.
* Maintain control networks, addressing, gateways, controller comms, diagnose comm loss and bus faults.
* Keep as-builts, riser diagrams, device schedules, and labeling current.

Facility Support, Documentation & Safety
  

* Support daily Facilities work orders, PMs, and guest impacting calls outside primary scope as assigned.
* Respond to after hours and emergency calls, power loss, panel trips, life safety lighting failures.
* Support event turnovers, contractor escort and inspection, and shutdown/restoration under senior engineering direction.
* Document all work in the CMMS, maintain panel schedules and as-builts, support egress and emergency lighting testing records.

**QUALIFICATIONS:**  
Required
  

* BS/BE in Electrical Engineering or EET.
* 0–3 years in electrical systems, building controls, or lighting. Internship, apprenticeship, or military experience counts.
* Working knowledge of the NEC, able to read electrical drawings, one lines, panel schedules, and control submittals.
* Hands on troubleshooting.
* Basic networking literacy.

Preferred
  

* EIT or passed FE exam.
* GRMS experience in hospitality.
* Programming or commissioning on a lighting control platform.
* Experience in a hotel, casino, resort, or other 24/7 environment.

**DESCRIPTION**
---------------

Application deadline: Oct 24, 2026  
  
Are you inspired by invention? Is problem solving through teamwork in your DNA? Do you like the idea of seeing how your work impacts the bigger picture? Answer yes to any of these and you'll fit right in here at Robotics Technical Services (RTS).  
  
We are a smart team of doers who work passionately to apply advances in robotics and software to solve real-world challenges that will transform our customers' experiences in ways we can't even imagine yet. The RTS Field Support team provides critical support to internal fulfillment and transportation network customers relying on advanced robotics technology.
  
  
You will be responsible for a technical product portfolio. In this role, you serve as the vital link between on-site technicians and RTS engineering teams, ensuring maximum performance of advanced robotics systems. You will launch new systems, develop preventative maintenance procedures, ensure spare part availability, proactively monitor system performance, provide troubleshooting support, and drive continuous improvement initiatives across Amazon's fulfillment network. You will establish standard operating procedures, performance metrics, and feedback mechanisms that enable the RTS team to scale effectively. Working closely with technical support teams and regional support managers, you will build a cohesive organization responsible for the safety, reliability, and performance of emerging robotics technology. This role requires independent judgment and comfort working with ambiguity in a complex, fast-paced, high-throughput environment where multi-tasking is essential.  
  
Key job responsibilities  

* Provide on-site support for new product implementations, upgrades, hardware audits, and troubleshooting for advanced robotics systems
* Partner with site-level reliability (RME) and controls teams to maximize advanced robotics system performance
* Identify, analyze, and resolve mechanical and system issues across the RTS product suite
* Design and implement electro-mechanical tools, fixtures, and diagnostic solutions to minimize troubleshooting and machine downtime
* Develop and implement proactive monitoring tools to measure safety, reliability, and performance of advanced robotics systems
* Create escalation processes, standard operating procedures, and preventative maintenance protocols for the RTS product suite
* Design and lead training sessions and develop training content for on-site RME teams
* Develop and implement spare parts management systems and processes
* Produce performance reports and provide "voice of the customer" feedback to development and support teams
* Up to 75% travel expected

Your day begins by reviewing system performance reports for your regional portfolio. Perhaps the metrics dashboard revealed unusual performance at a facility or spare parts dropped below threshold at a site. You analyze metrics to identify trends and risks, developing de-risking actions for leadership's weekly business review. You troubleshoot with RME technicians via video, walking them through diagnostic procedures. On-site, you conduct hardware audits for new deployments, gathering customer feedback. Afternoons include designing tools, optimizing processes, and coordinating with regional managers on scaling strategies. Throughout, you're the critical link between field technicians and engineering teams. Every member on the team leverages AI to drive efficiency and most build with it; you will be provided ample learning resources and challenges to demonstrate your skillset.

We’re the leading technology company in an industry most people drive past without thinking about. **Systems Software Engineer, Hardware Validation**

**About us:**

Voyant Photonics builds silicon photonic chips that steer and switch light at high speed. They power next generation, chip-scale FMCW LiDAR for robotics and autonomy, and optical circuit switches (OCS) for AI data centers. Based in NYC, we’re a hands-on team designing, building, and deploying frontier hardware to solve problems that matter, from how machines see to how AI scales.

**About the role**

Our tech stack spans FPGA and ASIC logic, microcontroller firmware, Linux drivers and cross platform user-facing APIs, and every layer changes every week. We're hiring engineers, at more than one level, to keep them integrated, tested and releasable.

**What Actually Matters**

Code is cheaper to write than ever. Knowing what should be written, and what "done" means, is the job. We want someone with strong, well-reasoned opinions about how software should be organized and how test coverage should grow, who argues for them, and who changes their mind when the evidence says so.

Things we believe in as a team:

* **Fix it at the source.** A bug gets fixed where it lives, even when that's someone else's code. The friction of working in each other's areas is worth it.
* **Live at the tip.** Every repo tracks the latest of everything it depends on. Small, frequent bumps surface breaks while they're still cheap to fix.
* **Duplicated code is broken code.** Two copies drift apart, and then one of them is wrong.
* **It doesn't work until someone else has run it on hardware.** Your own simulation or bench is where you start, not where you're done.

Disagree with one? Tell us why when you apply.

**What You'll Do**

* Own releases from commit to customer: build, verify, version and ship product bundles (FPGA bitstreams, firmware, drivers, APIs), including field updates, with release notes and runbooks people trust.
* Grow our HIL CI to cover every subsystem, and bring each new product into it from its first bring-up board.
* Track every bug CI finds to its root cause, whether that's Python, Rust, firmware, a Linux driver or FPGA logic, then fix it.
* Take our products into the systems that use them: time sync, calibration, sensor fusion, and open-source ecosystems like OCP and ROS.

**What We're Looking For**

* 2+ years of software engineering experience, or equivalent depth from research, internships or serious personal projects. We'll scale scope to experience.
* Strong Python, and comfort debugging languages you don't write every day.
* Hands-on hardware experience: bring-up, reading schematics, and using lab instruments to tell a software bug from a board bug.
* CI/CD experience, ideally against real hardware.
* Proactive communicator who cares about documentation to support cross functional team members & customers.

**Nice to Have**

* Rust, C++ or embedded C (we use STM32)
* Linux device drivers, especially SPI and custom low-level interfaces
* Reading System Verilog well enough to debug across the FPGA boundary
* HIL rigs and lab automation (SCPI/VISA, self-hosted CI runners)
* Timing and signal-integrity debug across SPI, I2C, UART, Ethernet and JTAG/SWD, plus board rework
* Fiber optics and optical test equipment
* Datacenter networking, PTP, point clouds or ROS 2
* Supporting software that external customers depend on

**What You'll Gain**

* Ownership of the release and test architecture for our products, from first bring-up to shipping: real decisions, not someone else's pipeline.
* Close collaboration with hardware, optics, signal processing and perception engineers, and real influence over technical direction at an early-stage company.
* A path toward customer-facing integration work, if that interests you.

**Life at Voyant**

We build frontier hardware & software from our lab and office in Midtown Manhattan, where optical tables, lab benches and electronics sit alongside traditional office space. Our work is hands-on and primarily in person, but we don’t run on a rigid 9-to-5. We partner with customers across time zones, so some calls start early or run late, and we adjust schedules around them. We run a high-trust, high-accountability environment: you’ll own meaningful work, move quickly and often wear more than one hat. Voyant provides catered lunch every day at HQ, and we’re a diverse group of food lovers from around the world who enjoy sharing food, culture and technical ideas around the lunch table.

**Equal Opportunity Employer**

Voyant Photonics is an equal opportunity employer committed to building a diverse and inclusive workplace. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and do not discriminate based on race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, pregnancy, marital or partnership status, age, national origin, citizenship, veteran or military status, disability, medical condition, genetic information, caregiver status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

Compensation Range: $110K - $170K

* Strong understanding of electrical standards (NEC, UL 508A, NFPA 70E / 79, MIL-HDBK-454).
* Hands-on experience with motor control centers (MCCs), VFDs, sensor technology, and safety circuits.

* Lake front Campus with amenities including fire pits, outdoor grills, pickleball and basketball courts, frisbee golf course, paddleboards, and lakeside trails

Our BIOS engineers solve complex firmware challenges and build robust, secure bootloader solutions that enable AWS to maintain its competitive edge in cloud computing.  
  
The ideal candidate will be an innovative self-starter with deep expertise in UEFI/BIOS development. You will be a firmware specialist with comprehensive knowledge of x86 and ARM64 architecture, secure boot implementations, and low-level system programming. You will gain intimate understanding of AWS's custom server firmware stack and analyze it for both current needs and future scalability. Ready to make connectivity from space universally accessible, secure and actionable? Then you’ve come to the right place!

E-Space is bridging Earth and space to enable hyper-scaled deployments of Internet of Things (IoT) solutions and services. We are building a highly-advanced low Earth orbit (LEO) space system that will fundamentally change the design, economics, manufacturing and service delivery associated with traditional satellite and terrestrial IoT systems.

We’re intentional, we’re unapologetically curious and we’re 100% committed to innovate space-based communications and deliver actionable intelligence that will expand global economies, protect space and our planet and enhance our overall quality of life.

  

Join us to design and deploy next-generation, satellite-based radar that delivers persistent, all-weather, day-night sensing at global scale. You’ll build end-to-end capabilities—from waveform design, on-board processing, classification and calibration—for systems on LEO platforms. Working across RF hardware, phased arrays, and advanced DSP, you’ll turn raw echoes into decision-ready products. If you thrive at the intersection of electromagnetics, signal processing, and systems engineering—and want your code and designs to fly—this role is for you.

### **What you’ll be doing:**

* Develop RF requirements and budgets for gain, noise, dynamic range, linearity, phase, timing, spurious response, and interference.

* Model and analyze antenna-to-digitizer and transmit/receive signal-chain performance.

* Define calibration, monitoring, built-in test, and fault-isolation approaches.

* Coordinate with array hardware, FPGA, embedded, signal processing, mechanical, power, thermal, and test teams.

* Support component selection, supplier reviews, lab characterization, design reviews, and anomaly resolution.

### **What you bring to this role:**

* Bachelor's or advanced degree in electrical engineering and 6+ years of RF/microwave system engineering.

* Experience with RF budgets, phased arrays, receivers/transmitters, converters, calibration, and laboratory measurements.

* Proficiency with RF simulation and test tools.

* Ability to translate system performance into component and interface requirements.

* Security clearance: U.S. citizenship is required. Candidate must be able to obtain and maintain a U.S. Government security clearance at the Secret level or higher, and any program-specific access required for the position. Continued employment is contingent upon obtaining and maintaining the required clearance and access.

### **Bonus points for the following:**

* UHF radar and high-dynamic-range direct-sampling experience.

* EMI/EMC, interference mitigation, spectrum certification, or environmental qualification experience.

* Experience with large channel-count systems.

This is a full time, exempt position, based out of our Saratoga office. The target base pay for this position is $120,000 - $200,000 annually. The total compensation packaged will be determined by various factors such as your relevant job-related knowledge, skills, and experience.

We are redefining how satellites are designed, manufactured and used—so we’re looking for candidates with passion, deep knowledge and direct experience on LEO satellite component development, design and in-orbit activities. If that’s your experience – then we’ll be immediately wow-ed.

This role requires access to controlled technical data. Under U.S. law (ITAR/EAR), we can only consider U.S. persons (U.S. citizens, lawful permanent residents, and individuals granted asylum or refugee status).

**Why E-Space is right for you:**

As a member of our team, you will play a crucial role in driving our success. Our team members have a strong sense of dedication and responsibility; this includes a strong commitment to our mission to create an entirely new suite of global capabilities to improve lives, business efficiencies and build a smarter planet. This means that there will be times when extra hours, including nights and weekends, may be needed to meet critical deadlines and mission goals. In return, we offer a dynamic work environment with opportunities for professional growth and development and the chance to make a meaningful impact in a high-growth industry.

  

We want you to make the most of your journey at E-Space. That’s why we support and invest in the physical, emotional and financial well-being of our team members and their families. Some of what you can expect when working at E-Space:

new_jobs.title: Senior Security Software Engineer, Datacenter Infrastructure Security
new_jobs.description:
We are the Foundational Security team in Apple Services Engineering (ASE). We secure the low-level foundations of Apple's datacenter fleet: hardware-backed trust, disk encryption, and the systems used to manage every server below the operating system.  
  
We're looking for a senior engineer to take technical ownership of the platform that manages our baseboard management controllers. You'll set its engineering and security bar, shape how access is granted and verified, and lead its move toward modern, standards-based management. You'll work closely with datacenter operations, SRE, hardware, network and detection teams, and become the go-to expert on managing Apple's fleet securely.  
  
**Description**  
  
This role owns the design, code and security of a privileged, availability-critical service. You'll write and review production code. You'll find and remove risk in how the service authenticates users, authorizes them and handles credentials, and you'll make privileged activity visible to the teams who detect misuse. You'll also help modernize how the fleet is managed, bringing along the many internal teams and tools that depend on the platform.  
  
Over time, you'll help define what secure out-of-band management looks like at Apple. That includes how access is segmented across environments, how firmware is delivered and trusted, and what we require of management controllers in future hardware. It also includes how access should work when the requester is an automated system rather than a person.  
  
**Preferred Qualifications**  
  
Hands-on experience with server management technologies such as IPMI, DMTF Redfish, OpenBMC, or vendor BMCs (e.g., HPE iLO, Dell iDRAC)  
  
Experience finding and fixing security flaws in networked services through code review, threat modeling or security testing  
  
A track record of technical leadership: driving architecture decisions and cross-team migrations, mentoring engineers, and explaining security trade-offs to engineers and leadership  
  
Experience with gRPC and Protocol Buffers, and with running PostgreSQL in production  
  
Experience managing the lifecycle of secrets and credentials at fleet scale, including rotation and emergency access  
  
Experience building and operating highly available, distributed services that other teams depend on  
  
Familiarity with network segmentation and zero-trust access patterns, such as identity-aware proxies  
  
Knowledge of firmware security, including secure boot, firmware signing and updates, TPMs and hardware roots of trust  
  
Hands-on experience using AI coding assistants on a production codebase

Tesla's Optimus program is building a future of sustainable abundance and we are building a team that designs and builds the automated manufacturing machines. You and your team will architect, develop and deploy software for industrial controllers, like PLCs, HMIs, robot controllers, machine vision systems and more. New automated manufacturing equipment is designed, built and performance tested by us, then set up at its final destination for final commissioning and start of production.

new_jobs.description:
##### **About Peraton**

Peraton is a next-generation national security company that drives missions of consequence spanning the globe and extending to the farthest reaches of the galaxy. As the world’s leading mission capability integrator and transformative enterprise IT provider, we deliver trusted, highly differentiated solutions and technologies to protect our nation and allies. Peraton operates at the critical nexus between traditional and nontraditional threats across all domains: land, sea, space, air, and cyberspace. The company serves as a valued partner to essential government agencies and supports every branch of the U.S. armed forces. Each day, our employees solve the most daunting challenges that our customers face. Visit peraton.com to learn how we’re keeping people around the world safe and secure.

##### **About The Role**

Peraton provides management and technical support for NASA’s scientific balloon program which supports enabling science missions for NASA and universities across the United States and foreign scientific communities. Scientific balloon missions provide researchers inexpensive, relatively quick, long duration access to near space altitudes and environments. Balloon missions cost orders of magnitude less than satellite missions and provide platforms for heavy experiments (some greater than 5000-lbs) to operate for weeks and even months. Balloon missions have provided significant science theories and discoveries about cosmic rays, gamma ray and x-ray astronomy, optical and UV astronomy, atmospheric sciences, and cosmic microwave background studies.

  

Our staff are located at the Columbia Scientific Balloon Facility (CSBF) in Palestine, TX where we design, analyze, build and assembly the support hardware and balloon gondola payloads for the missions. We launch the balloons from locations within the United States (Texas, New Mexico, and Hawaii) and around the world including Antarctica, Sweden, New Zealand, and Australia. Our engineers and technician staff support the launches and balloon and payload recoveries in the US and many worldwide locations. Peraton’s NASA Balloon Operations Contract (NBOC) program is seeking a candidate to support manufacture, test, integration, and field operations for NASA Balloon missions.

  

Our rural campus offers the ability to work in a low-cost of living area, but within an easy drive of Tyler, Dallas and Houston.

Responsibilities for the position:

* Support the NASA Scientific Balloon Program in the use of electrical circuits, assemblies, and devices for a variety of applications including balloon flight hardware, ground support hardware, test equipment, and/or facility modifications
* Perform complex integration ant testing of electronic systems
* Plan the manufacture, installation, operation, and maintenance of electrical apparatus
* Work directly with engineers in other disciplines in system development and integration
* Act as internal consultant providing technical guidance on complex projects
* Design, fabricate, test, verify, and integrate electrical systems
* Assess technical specifications and issue procurement requests; attend meetings, write and deliver reports and presentations to clients and managers
* Prepare design documentation including technical text, illustrations, tables, and schematics
* Draw plans and specifications for projects using computer assisted engineering and design software
* Estimate material, construction, and labor costs with project timescales
* Test installations / systems; analyze data observing all applicable electrical / construction safety regulations

Must be able to travel up to 60% travel

##### **Qualifications**

Required Qualifications:

* Bachelor of Science in Electrical Engineering or Engineering Technology degree
* Five of more years of experience
* Willingness and ability to mentor junior employees and coworkers
* Understanding of test installations and familiar with test equipment
* Experience in digital circuit design
* Experience with configuration, troubleshooting, and operation RF telemetry system hardware
* Experience with troubleshooting and repair of analog circuitry and hardware
* Experience with failure mode analysis and root cause identification
* Experience with Orcad Capture or equivalent schematic/design software
* Experience with SOLIDWORKS or equivalent 3D modeling software
* Ability to maintain professional and effective communication while interacting with other disciplines and external customers.
* Must be able to pass a background check and drug screening. Must be able to obtain a NASA PIV badge.
* Must be a US Citizen.

Desired Qualifications:

* Experience in Electrical engineering and signal conditioning design
* Knowledge and experience with ordnance safety and handling
* ISO J-STD- 001 Requirements for Soldered Electrical and Electronic Assemblies
* ISO/WHMA-A-620 Requirements and Acceptance for Cable and Wire Harness Assemblies
  

Specific Requirements / Licensing Special Requirements:

* Must be able to travel to support campaigns in various locations around the world
* Must have or be able to obtain a passport
* Must pass the National Science Foundation Physical (Medical) requirement to work in Antarctica

##### **Details**

**Target Salary Range:** $80,000 - $128,000. This represents the typical salary range for this position. Salary is determined by various factors, including but not limited to, the scope and responsibilities of the position, the individual’s experience, education, knowledge, skills, and competencies, as well as geographic location and business and contract considerations. * Oversee the alignment of terrestrial sensor systems with the Intelligence/SIGINT/Cyber enterprise, ensuring local sensor data is ingestible by advanced analytics platforms and cloud environments.

* Bachelors and nine (9) years or more experience; Masters and seven (7) years or more experience ; PhD or JD and four (4) years or more experience.

We are seeking an experienced **Lead Network Automation Engineer** to lead the development, implementation, and sustainment of network automation solutions supporting a complex, multivendor enterprise network environment.

  
  

The ideal candidate combines strong network engineering fundamentals with advanced hands on expertise in Python and Ansible. This individual will collaborate closely with network administrators, engineers, architects, and customer stakeholders to translate technical requirements into scalable, reliable, and maintainable automation solutions.

This is a hands on technical leadership position responsible for developing production ready automation, mentoring a small team of automation engineers, and helping establish repeatable engineering practices.

  
  

The successful candidate will play a critical role in improving network operational efficiency, accelerating configuration deployments, reducing manual effort, and increasing the consistency and reliability of network infrastructure operations.

  
  

**Key Responsibilities:**

  
  

**Network Automation Engineering**

* Design, develop, test, deploy, and maintain network automation solutions using Python and Ansible.

* Automate network device configuration changes, software updates, configuration backups, compliance checks, and operational validation across multivendor environments.
* Develop automation capabilities supporting Cisco, Juniper, Arista, Aruba, and other enterprise networking technologies.
* Implement automated configuration validation, network state verification, and configuration drift detection to improve network reliability and compliance.
* Build automation solutions for network monitoring, reporting, inventory management, and operational data collection.
* Develop standardized, reusable automation components that reduce repetitive administrative activities and improve engineering consistency.
* Incorporate appropriate error handling, logging, validation, and rollback capabilities into automated network changes.

* Conduct code reviews and promote consistent development, testing, documentation, and version control practices.
* Establish reusable development standards and promote knowledge sharing across the automation team.
* Support the development of junior and midlevel engineers through technical coaching and collaborative problem solving.
* Communicate progress, technical challenges, dependencies, and delivery risks to engineering and program leadership.

**Automation Capability Development and Sustainment**

* Develop maintainable automation solutions that can be supported and enhanced by other engineers.
* Assist with implementing appropriate development, testing, and production deployment controls.

**Technical Qualifications**

new_jobs.description:
**About Globe Machine**

For over 100 years, Globe Machine Manufacturing has delivered custom-engineered capital equipment for manufacturers in the pulp & paper, building products, and advanced composites industries. Globe is known for designing and building large-scale material handling and material moving systems-including conveyors, stackers, and integrated production machinery-supported by automation, controls, and robotics.

**Role Overview**

The Systems Engineer leads the design and execution of Globe's mechanical equipment solutions while managing and developing a team of engineers. This role is both hands-on and strategic-responsible for guiding mechanical design, ensuring technical excellence, and delivering complex industrial equipment that meets customer, manufacturing, and commercial requirements.

This is a key leadership role within Globe's engineering organization, working closely with Project Management, Operations, Controls, and Sales.

This position is located in Tacoma, WA.

**What You'll Do as Systems Engineer**

**Lead Mechanical Engineering Teams**

* Lead, mentor, and develop a team of mechanical engineers focused on capital equipment and material handling systems.
* Provide technical direction, design oversight, and coaching across projects.
* Support workload planning, resource allocation, and project prioritization.

**Design & Deliver Capital Equipment**

* Oversee the mechanical design of conveyors, stackers, and other industrial equipment used in heavy manufacturing environments.
* Review and approve designs, calculations, layouts, and specifications.
* Ensure designs meet performance, safety, manufacturability, and cost targets.

**Technical Oversight & Problem Solving**

* Lead complex technical problem-solving and root-cause analysis.
* Guide engineering decisions related to materials, mechanisms, structural integrity, and system performance.
* Support installation planning and resolve field or commissioning challenges as needed.

**Cross-Functional Collaboration**

* Partner closely with Project Management to support schedules, budgets, and execution.
* Collaborate with Operations and Manufacturing to ensure designs are production ready.
* Work with Sales and Customer-facing teams to support technical scoping and customer requirements.

**Process & Continuous Improvement**

* Drive engineering best practices, standards, and documentation.
* Improve design processes, tools, and workflows to support scalability and quality.

**What Makes You a Great Fit**

You are a mechanical engineering leader who enjoys both designing industrial equipment and leading people. You've worked on large, custom machines-not small consumer products-and understand what it takes to deliver reliable capital equipment in demanding industrial environments.

**Required Skills & Experience**

* Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering or closely related discipline
* 7+ years of experience designing industrial machinery, capital equipment, or material handling systems
* Proven experience leading or managing mechanical engineering teams
* Strong background in mechanical design for heavy industrial applications
* Proficiency with CAD tools (Inventor, SolidWorks, AutoCAD or similar)
* Strong communication skills and ability to work cross-functionally

**Preferred Experience**

* Experience with conveyors, stackers, or large material moving systems
* Exposure to automation, controls, or integrated manufacturing systems
* Experience working in OEM or custom equipment environments
* Familiarity with manufacturing processes and design-for-manufacturing principles

**Why Globe**

At Globe, engineering leadership matters. You'll have the opportunity to lead meaningful work-designing large-scale equipment that directly supports critical industries-while helping shape the future of Globe's engineering organization.

new_jobs.title: Senior Communication Systems Engineer
new_jobs.description:
Description:

**About Chartis Federal**

Chartis Federal is a premier systems engineering and integration firm specializing in mission-critical IT and communications solutions for law enforcement, homeland security, and defense. As a trusted prime contractor with over $160 million in task order awards, we operate across 22 states and support essential government missions worldwide.

Our commitment to excellence has fueled our year-over-year growth, earning us recognition twice as a Washington Technology FAST 50 company and securing a place on the Inc. 5000 list for five consecutive years. At Chartis Federal, our mission is clear: keeping heroes safe and connected—on the battlefield, on the border, and in our backyards.

**Position Overview**

Chartis is seeking a Senior Communications Systems Engineer, able to obtain a Public Trust clearance, to provide Systems Engineering Technical Assistance (SETA) support to our customer’s Disaster Emergency Communications Division (DECD). This role works on high-visibility, mission-critical aspects of the program, evaluating, designing, and documenting the fixed, mobile, and tactical communications systems that support federal disaster response. This position will be hybrid (onsite 2 days a week, with potential to be fully onsite).

**Responsibilities**

* Continuously evaluate technological advancements in Federal, State, Local, Tribal, and Territorial (FSLTT) communications equipment capabilities and anticipated requirements.
* Provide Systems Engineering Technical Assistance (SETA) to update the Tactical End-State Architecture (TESA) and develop strategic initiatives for the continued refresh and life-cycle management of communications technology supporting response missions.
* Assess how existing capabilities can meet FSLTT communications requirements, drawing on State Emergency Communications Annexes and Regional Emergency Communications Plans (RECPs).
* Evaluate 5-year anticipated technology trends to update technology roadmaps and communications strategic plans, and recommend improvements to FEMA’s capabilities in support of its disaster response mission.
* Provide expert-level technical, engineering, and CAD/GIS support to conduct baseline analysis, documentation, and engineering diagrams and schematics for fixed, mobile, and tactical communications assets.
* Support communications systems including satellite, radio frequency (RF), LTE, broadband, Next Generation 911 (NG911), and the development of FirstNet systems, and evaluate emerging technologies such as 5G, high-throughput satellite (HTS), and low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite.
* Perform RF propagation analysis and modeling, site surveys, and technical evaluation of emerging technologies.
* Evaluate program adherence to federal and agency policies and regulations.
* Develop executive-level reports and briefings on technology trends and their implications for disaster emergency communications.
* Perform all functional duties independently on high-visibility, mission-critical aspects of the program, and oversee the efforts of less senior staff as needed.
* Other specific duties as assigned.

Requirements:

* Master’s degree (MA/MS) in Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, or a closely related field; more than 10 years of progressively relevant communications engineering experience.
* Must be a U.S. Citizen and able to obtain and maintain a Public Trust security clearance.
* Demonstrated ability to perform RF propagation analysis and modeling, site surveys, and technical evaluation of emerging technologies.
* Experience with communications systems and architectures, including satellite, RF, land mobile radio (LMR), high frequency (HF), LTE, broadband, NG911, and FirstNet.
* Experience producing engineering diagrams, schematics, and baseline documentation; CAD/GIS experience a plus.
* Excellent oral and written communication skills, including the ability to develop executive-level reports.
* Ability to interact and network effectively with all levels of staff, including technical and non-technical senior leadership.
* Strong problem-solving skills with the ability to foresee the direct and indirect impacts of solutions.
* Innovative thinker who brings new ideas to the team; flexible and adaptable.
* Ability to meet deadlines, adhere to project plans, bring conflicts to the attention of the management team, and work on several projects simultaneously.
* Willingness to travel (approximately 15% or less).
* Proficiency in Microsoft Office, including Word, Excel, Microsoft Teams, and PowerPoint.
* Professional Engineer (PE) license and prior experience supporting FEMA, DHS, or public safety communications programs preferred.

**Why Join Chartis Federal?**

We offer a competitive compensation and benefits package, including:

* Comprehensive health insurance (medical, dental, vision)
* Retirement plans with company contributions
* Professional development opportunities and career growth support
* A dynamic and collaborative work environment where your contributions are valued

At Chartis Federal, we believe in fostering a culture of excellence, integrity, and innovation while supporting critical national security missions. Join us in shaping the future of government contracting and national security solutions.

Chartis Federal is an Equal Opportunity Employer and employs qualified individuals regardless of race, religion, color, sex, national origin, age, disability, or any other classification protected under applicable law. We participate in E-Verify.

**Job Description**

We have an exciting opportunity for a **Lead Software Engineer** at UL Research Institutes , within our Digital Safety Research Institute (DSRI) . Th is is a REMOTE opportunity

The **Lead Software Engineer** is a major contributor to the development and maintenance of complex software systems of Digital Safety. The Lead Software Engineer provides technical guidance, mentorship, and leadership to the team while collaborating with stakeholders to deliver high-quality software solutions.

**UL** **Research Institute** **s:**

At UL Research Institutes (ULRI) , we expand the boundaries of safety science to create a more secure and sustainable world. For more than a century, we have studied the unintended consequences of innovation, designed solutions to mitigate risk and shared our findings with academia, scientists, manufacturers, and policymakers across industries. We identify critical safety and sustainability issues, asking tough questions because we believe a safer world begins with knowledge.

**Digital Safety Research Institute:**

The Digital Safety Research Institute (DSRI) addresses unresolved safety risks and emerging dangers in the world’s digital ecosystem. We aim to help protect people from unwanted access to personal devices and privacy, algorithms , and disinformation threats by working to create a new digital safety ecosystem.

DSRI is committed to sharing digital safety insights, collaborating with key stakeholders, and offering extensive outreach and education to help support safer digital environments for people everywhere.

**What** **you’ll** **learn** **and** **achieve:**

As the **Lead Software** **Engineer,** you will play a key role in the rapid growth of UL as you:

* Lead, define, and develop full-stack software systems and platforms that enable large-scale research, evaluation, and dissemination of safety insights

* Implement service boundaries, data model evolution, integration patterns between our platforms, and the pipelines and evaluation frameworks they feed

* Set technical direction across projects, aligning architecture and data frameworks with DSRI’s evolving research priorities and the broader AI evaluation ecosystem

* Iterative design of complex, ambiguous, cross-cutting systems where the problem isn’t fully understood

* Ensure consistency in engineering practices and set the standard for AI-assisted engineering on the team, including the use of Claude Code on large refactors, greenfield work, and adopted code from external organizations; developing patterns and documentation to accelerate software engineering.

* Provide feedback to teams using AI coding tools in a dangerous, inappropriate, or inefficient way.

* Provide guidance and informal mentorship to junior engineers to support skill development and knowledge sharing.

* Foster a collaborative and positive work environment, promote knowledge sharing and professional growth within the team.

* Assist in hiring, onboarding, and training new software engineers, ensuring a smooth integration into the team.

* Represent technical work across the organization and in select external settings

* Contribute to and/or lead other department specific and cross-functional initiatives.

**What makes you a great fit:**

**While no one candidate will embody every quality, the successful candidate will bring many of the following professional competencies and personal attributes** **:**

* Deep expertise in software engineering, applied across the systems that support research and data-driven analysis (i.e., React in production at meaningful scale or complexity, Python services, async patterns, careful data handling, sensible API design, PostgreSQL, designing and implementing complex data structures, and working knowledge of the systems layer underneath, including containers, deployment, and observability).

* Architectural judgment built on real experience (i.e., able to make choices from experience and articulate trade-offs, and able to know when not to introduce a new service, abstraction, or dependency).

* Sophisticated use of AI coding tools, including integrating Claude Code or similar tools into substantial, non-trivial work and the ability to structure context, decompose problems, review generated code, and recover when the tools do not function properly.

* Track record of technical leadership without formal authority, with experience raising the level of teams through what you build and how you work.

* Clear, direct written communication and the ability to translate complex technical work for varied audiences (i.e., design documents, RFCs, post-mortems, asynchronous code reviews, and internal and external presentations).

* Genuine interest in AI safety, test & evaluation, or one of specific harm domains (e.g., synthetic media, chatbot safety

**Professional education and experience requirements for the role include:**

* Bachelor’s degree in computer science, or equivalent combination of education and experience. Master’s degree preferred.

* Minimum 8 years of experience in software development, with a focus on platform security and proficiency in multiple programming languages and frameworks.

* Experience deploying several complex software products and understands the nuances of the software development life cycle.
